# Fixture sources

The HTML paper and publisher-gate fixtures are synthetic representations with standard citation metadata, section and bibliography shapes. Their text is original test data; document identifiers are used to exercise routing and metadata contracts. Discussion fixtures retain representative Redlib DOM shapes and score/loading evidence but use synthetic comment and author text. Marketplace fixtures use synthetic listing identifiers.

`scholar_epmc_jats.xml` contains John P. A. Ioannidis, "Why Most Published Research Findings Are False," PLOS Medicine (2005), [doi:10.1371/journal.pmed.0020124](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pmed.0020124). The embedded [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) notice and attribution are retained. Contact addresses have been replaced with placeholders. This article is licensed separately from OmniRead's Apache-2.0 code.

Bibliographic JSON fixtures contain work metadata from Crossref, OpenAlex, Unpaywall, Europe PMC and bioRxiv. They are used as parser inputs and do not grant access to the papers they describe. No fixture establishes completeness across the live web.
